title: Predictive-prefetch vs tiling vs opportunistic slots: latency & cost scan
body:
Summary:
This short working brief captures a compact benchmark comparing three runtime strategies for sessionized conversational workloads: predictive-prefetch (simple predictor + KV warmup), windowed-tiling (fixed-length tiling with slot packing), and opportunistic-slots (on-demand multiplex with slot stealing). Focus: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms) for single-turn generation, and amortized cost per 1k tokens for steady and burst traffic shapes.

Key takeaways (high-level):
- Predictive-prefetch reduces p50 by ~12-18% relative to opportunistic-slots for conversational turns with high locality, while increasing steady cost by ~4-7% due to extra warmed KV traffic.
- Windowed-tiling gives the best p95/p99 stability under sustained concurrency (lower variance) but can increase p50 slightly compared to predictive-prefetch if tiling granularity is coarse.
- Opportunistic-slots is cheapest at low sustained QPS (no wasted warmups) but suffers most in burst microbursts (p99 uplift).
- Recommendation: hybrid policy that uses predictive-prefetch for identified high-locality customer cohorts, windowed-tiling for reserved/high-throughput pools, and opportunistic-slots as fallback to minimize idle cost.

Methodology (short):
- Workload: synthetic conversation traces derived from production session mix (70% short-turn (<=40 tokens), 20% medium (40-150), 10% long (>150)). Inter-arrival distribution matches sessionized cadence (heavy tail microbursts).
- Model: open-llama-7b-quant equivocation path (approx cost/latency comparable to our 7B quant profiles).
- Hardware: single A100-80GB equivalence node (baseline), with multiplexing slots simulated per current runtime semantics.
- Configurations:
  1) predictive-prefetch: predictor uses last-turn embedding + simple LRU-hotlist; prefetch initiated if predictor score > 0.6; KV warmup limit = 3 sequences per slot.
  2) windowed-tiling: tiles = 64-token windows, pack up to 6 tiles per slot, slot-hold-time = 120s before eviction.
  3) opportunistic-slots: no prefetch, dynamic slot allocation, slot-hold-time = 30s.
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 response time for generation start-to-first-token (milliseconds), and amortized GPU-ms per 1k tokens converted to $/1k tokens using internal kernel-cost curve. 30 runs per scenario, 1-hour simulated time windows.

Aggregate results (median of runs):

Latency table (ms):
Scenario                 | p50  | p95  | p99  | p99 - p50 delta
-------------------------+------+-------+------+----------------
Predictive-prefetch      | 85   | 210   | 330  | 245
Windowed-tiling          | 92   | 185   | 260  | 168
Opportunistic-slots      | 105  | 240   | 410  | 305

Cost table (amortized):
Scenario                 | $/1k tokens (steady) | $/1k tokens (microburst 10x)
-------------------------+----------------------+----------------------------
Predictive-prefetch      | 1.12                 | 1.45                       
Windowed-tiling          | 1.08                 | 1.40                       
Opportunistic-slots      | 0.98                 | 1.72                       

Notes on numbers: predictive-prefetch increases baseline cost by ~14% vs opportunistic in steady state but reduces p50 by ~19% (105 -> 85 ms). Under 10x microburst, opportunistic cost shoots up due to inefficient cold starts and slot churn; predictive-prefetch & tiling both amortize warmed state better.

ASCII microburst latency profile (p99 over time sample, normalized):
Time(s)   0    5    10   15   20   25   30
PredictPF 1.0  1.1  1.05 1.02 1.00 1.01 0.98
Tiling    1.0  1.03 1.02 1.00 0.99 1.00 0.98
Opportun  1.0  1.6  2.1  2.0  1.8  1.4  1.1
(Interpretation: opportunistic spikes early then slowly recovers; tiling and predictive are flatter.)

Failure modes observed (qualitative):
- Predictor false-positives: prefetching cold sessions that never hit the KV, wasted warmup cost. This shows up as cost inflation with no latency benefit for low-locality sessions.
- Tiling fragmentation: with heterogeneous turn lengths, fixed tile windows either underutilize slots (waste) or increase p50 when we wait to fill tiles.
- Slot eviction thrash: short slot-hold times with opportunistic slots cause repeated kernel/context reloads leading to p99 tail and cost spikes.

Sensitivity experiments (abbreviated):
- Increasing predictor threshold from 0.6 -> 0.8: reduces prefetch wasted cost by ~40% but cuts latency benefit (p50 improves only ~6% vs opportunistic).
- Tile size sweep (32/64/128): 32 gives best p50 but worst steady cost; 128 best steady cost but worsens p50 when session mix has many short turns. 64 is near Pareto for our mix.
- Slot-hold time: moving opportunistic from 30s -> 90s reduces p99 by ~22% but increases steady cost ~9%.

Operational recommendations (actionable):
- Implement a cohorting signal: apply predictive-prefetch only to customer cohorts with >40% locality (measured by last-7-day KV reuse). Default to opportunistic for <20% locality.
- Adopt 64-token windowed-tiling for Dedicated pools where throughput and p99 are prioritized; tune slot-hold-time to 120s.
- Expose predictor-threshold as a runtime knob in Console Optimize so teams can trade cost vs latency per route.
- Add a lightweight telemetry event: prefetch_decision -> outcome (hit/miss) so we can track prefetch ROI per route.

Appendix A — short example trace (annotated):
- Session A (high locality): predictor -> true, prefetch warms KV for turn 2 -> observed p50 62ms (vs 110ms opportunistic). Prefetch cost: +0.06$/1k tokens for this session type. Net ROI: 35% latency improvement for cohort; positive for UX heavy customers.
- Session B (low locality): predictor -> false positive, prefetch wasted; p50 unchanged, cost +0.09$/1k tokens. For low-locality customers, predictive-prefetch is net-negative.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Can we cheaply derive per-route locality score in Console without heavy instrumentation? (approximate via session-level embedding reuse rate + last-30-day KV-hit ratio).
- Should we prototype an adaptive hybrid that dynamically flips policy per minute based on recent hit-rate? Cost of gating logic vs benefits unknown.
- Need to re-run at 2x and 4x model sizes (13B, 70B quant proxies) to check how kernel setup costs amplify the observed deltas.

Short next steps (week):
- Add prefetch_decision outcome telemetry (Ravi) — sprint spike ticket created (INF-4123).
- Run 13B proxy sweep with same scenarios (Mei) — target by 2026-06-28.
- Draft console UX for per-route policy toggle + threshold (Liam) — lightweight mock by 2026-06-25.

This doc is a working brief; numbers are from internal sim harness and should be treated as directional. Comments welcome — especially on the cohort gating heuristic and how to present cost knobs in Console.
